verdict: ACCEPT -- 1 BLOCKING, 9 NON-BLOCKING. All three adjudicated repairs hold, and every one of them was re-derived here rather than read. Repair 2 was reproduced by an AST implementation written from scratch that agrees with the subject EXACTLY on both dependents and tools across the whole corpus. Repair 3 was reproduced at process level: the same real jq call leaves the predecessor at exit 0 and raises NPA-4-UNDECLARED-EXTERNAL-TOOL on the subject, and the containment counterfactual is measured -- `jq` occurs twice and `curl` three times in the environment-prerequisites section's own prose, so a containment test would have admitted precisely the tool the reviewer proved could be added undetected. Repair 1 holds and its contested design decision -- scoped skip rather than blanket refusal -- is vindicated by measurement rather than by argument: with v1-slice.md absent AND a real unrecorded disagreement planted in the blueprint, the run still reports that finding at exit 4, which a blanket exit-2 refusal would have thrown away. The BLOCKING finding is a route the LIMITS list does not name and the module docstring positively denies: NPA-5 exec(compile(...))s a SECOND module, artifacts/check-d9-v1.14.py, whose integrity is verified against a sha256 scraped from a plus/minus 400-character window around its own filename in the two UNPINNED documents under comparison. I replaced that module with attacker-chosen bytes, inserted one digest string into IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md, and the instrument executed the payload and printed a full green banner at exit 0. The file's own section headed WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO states 'It pins exactly ONE file, `check-package-coherence.py`, because it EXECUTES it.' It executes two.

I tested SEVEN out-of-vocabulary rewrites of the live heading -- 'Unsettled questions', 'Matters still in flight', 'To be resolved', 'Deferred items', 'Outstanding questions', 'Left for the product owner', 'Questions the slice does not answer'. ALL SEVEN produce exit 1 with 3 NPA-2-STALE-DISAGREEMENT-RECORD findings each. Never silence. 7 of 7.
L-1.halfTwo: L-1 claims symmetry CANNOT rescue a new, never-recorded disagreement under unknown vocabulary, because nothing goes stale. I built the matched control it describes: a genuinely binding, genuinely unrecorded row ('an implementation must build against the interim posture and must fail admission otherwise') placed under a NEW heading. Under '## 7. Unsettled questions' the run is EXIT 0 WITH NO FINDINGS -- completely invisible. The IDENTICAL row under '## 7. Open decisions' raises NPA-1-UNRECORDED-PACKET-DISAGREEMENT at exit 1. The gap is exactly as described, exactly as wide as described, and explicitly NOT claimed closed.
L-1.verdict: L-1's diagnosis is precise to the word: 'NOT CLOSED, and not claimed to be' and 'invisible in both directions'. My measurement matches its text with no residue. The mitigations it claims -- NPA-2 now diagnosing a zero-heading match, and the vocabulary plus per-document match counts printed in the banner -- are present and do exactly what is claimed, and are correctly described as making the gap LEGIBLE rather than closed.

selfReferenceAudit.rule: Freeze section 7.8.1: an instrument that hard-codes an example of what it hunts becomes an instance of it. The author records causing and removing exactly this regression twice in one night -- selftest probe strings injecting a phantom `jq` into a text census, and a hardcoded checker filename tripping the closure heuristic into self-attribution.
selfReferenceAudit.result: CLEAN. Both repairs hold under direct measurement.
evidence: The PREDECESSOR's text-regex census, run over a source set that INCLUDES the subject, attributes ZERO external tools to check-narrative-packet-agreement-v2.py. The probe fixtures are assembled at runtime (sp_call = "subprocess" + ".run"), so the literal the text scan needs never appears. The phantom-jq regression is gone and its absence is measured, not asserted.

The subject imports no subprocess: its full import set is __future__, ast, hashlib, importlib.util, inspect, json, pathlib, re, sys, typing. Its self-exclusion from its own NPA-4 census therefore removes an empty row under any predicate, exactly as the code comment claims.

The closure filename heuristic attributes ZERO execution edges to the subject. The subject IS exec-capable (it matches the exec(compile( trigger), and it names four peer checkers in prose, but none of them satisfies the quote-immediately-before-name pattern.

Hard-coded identifiers: `G3-SUBSTRATE` is synthetic and appears in no document. `A1-RI-04` and `rust-provider-protocol.v2` appear only in comments and LIMITS prose, never in a predicate. `P-1` appears in two selftest fixtures, and that is the one place a live corpus identifier is written into the instrument -- see NB-5.

blockers.title: The instrument EXECUTES a second module whose integrity is derived from a document under comparison, its LIMITS list names no route of this kind, and its docstring states the opposite.
blockers.site: check_npa_5, lines 1302-1335 (digest gathered at 1313-1318, exec at 1325-1330); the contradicted sentence is at line 200.
blockers.whatTheFileSays: Under the heading WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO: 'It pins exactly ONE file, `check-package-coherence.py`, because it EXECUTES it. Freeze section 7.3 permits executing a verified closure and requires the hash to hold BEFORE the bytes run. The order here is read, hash, compare, then exec.'
blockers.whatTheBytesDo: NPA-5 resolves the D9 contract's referenceDerivation to artifacts/check-d9-v1.14.py, reads it, computes its sha256, and compares that against the set of ALL 64-hex strings occurring within plus/minus 400 characters of ANY occurrence of the string 'check-d9-v1.14.py' in IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md or IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md. If the live digest is in that set, it exec(compile(...))s the module. Neither document is pinned -- correctly and deliberately, because they are the documents under comparison. So the authority to execute code is delegated to the surface the instrument exists to police.
blockers.measured: Executed, not argued. STEP 1: I appended an arbitrary side effect to artifacts/check-d9-v1.14.py and left the documents alone. The instrument REFUSED to run it -- exit 1, NPA-5-ORACLE-SIGNATURE-UNRECORDED, 'the D9 oracle on disk is not the one the package documents pin', and the payload did NOT execute. This is the correct fail-closed direction and is worth crediting. STEP 2: I left the same hostile bytes in place and inserted ONE string into IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md next to the module's name -- the new digest. Result: THE PAYLOAD EXECUTED (it wrote its marker file), NPA-5 raised NOTHING, and the run printed the full green banner at EXIT 0, including the line 'every document claim above equals the measurement it describes.'
blockers.whyItIsBlocking: Freeze section 7.1's own grading test is 'reachability on the actual bytes, not the category of the instrument', and section 7.8's standard for an instrument is 'for every assertion, exhibit an input that is WRONG rather than merely EMPTY'. This is a reachable green run over bytes the instrument chose to execute on a document's say-so, and the file's published account of its own execution surface is not merely incomplete -- it is false, in the section devoted to stating that surface. A reader who trusts that section will believe exactly one file's bytes are executed and will not know to check the second. That is freeze section 7.2.2's shape turned on the file's own bytes, and unlike prose asserting a JUDGEMENT it is a claim about bytes and therefore checkable, which section 7.8 says is precisely the kind an instrument must not get wrong.
blockers.notAnAdversaryOnlyProblem: The benign form matters more than the hostile one. IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md is a document implementers edit routinely and which this instrument is built to compare. An ordinary edit that records a stale or mistaken digest near that filename silently changes which bytes get executed, or -- more likely -- silently withdraws the authority to execute at all and converts NPA-5 into a finding about the oracle. Neither outcome is visible as what it is.
blockers.theInternalInconsistency: The file already knows the right shape and applies it eleven hundred lines earlier. check-package-coherence.py gets an INTERNAL pin in EXECUTED_PINS whose drift becomes a NAMED, non-fatal NPA-3-NOT-RUN skip at exit 4, and the file explicitly accepts the cost -- 'If the drift is a deliberate repair, a successor to THIS file re-pins it'. The stated reason for NOT doing this for the oracle is that 'a pin copied into this file would advance silently when the D9 head advances'. That reasoning is sound for a RECORDED-MEASUREMENT pin and is being applied to an EXECUTION gate, which is exactly the distinction freeze section 7.2.2 draws. It is also weaker than the argument the file already rejected: check-package-coherence.py is described in this same file as 'THE MOST MOVABLE CHECKER IN THE CORPUS' and is pinned internally anyway.
blockers.repairDirection: A successor, since section 7.2 forbids editing these bytes. Three things, and only the first is mandatory: (1) correct the WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO sentence to state that TWO files are executed and that the second's digest is derived from unpinned documents; (2) add the route to LIMITS, so the published escape count covers it and the existing staleness gate keeps it honest; (3) optionally take the digest from a source the instrument already reads as structured data and that is not one of the documents under comparison -- artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json already supplies the referenceDerivation and is a per-class input, so it could supply the digest too, giving the same advance-tolerance without delegating execution authority to prose.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The input tiering is not total: a per-class input that PARSES but has the wrong top-level shape escalates to a whole-run refusal at exit 2.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: artifacts/resolved-inputs.v2.json replaced with `[]` -- valid JSON, wrong shape. check_npa_6 calls resolved.get(...), AttributeError, caught by main's catch-all, output 'NPA-INTERNAL-ERROR: AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'', exit 2. The same happens for artifacts/product-dispositions.v1.json as `[]` or `null`, where exit 2 is the RIGHT tier but the token is a generic internal error rather than a named malformed-input refusal.
nonBlockingObservations.why: The published design is 'a PER-CLASS input that cannot be read SKIPS exactly the classes that need it'. A per-class input that is unreadable, absent or malformed JSON does exactly that (verified, 10 of 10 cases). A per-class input that is well-formed JSON of the wrong type does NOT: five classes that never needed the file stop measuring. The direction is safe -- never a traceback, never a false finding, and the operator is told the check did not run to completion -- so this is a shortfall against a published claim rather than a defect in the guarantee that matters. A shape guard at the two read_json call sites, or a Refusal raised on a non-dict top level, closes it.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The widened call surface is incomplete in a direction that matters, and the docstring's 'STRICTLY WIDER ... in the directions that matter' overstates it.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: SUBPROCESS_CALLS is ('run','Popen','check_output','check_call') and OS_SHELL_CALLS is ('system','popen'). With a LITERAL argv[0] and no indirection whatever, the following all return NOTHING from ast_direct_tools: subprocess.call(['jq','-r']); from subprocess import call; call(['jq']); subprocess.getoutput('jq -r .x'); subprocess.getstatusoutput('jq .x'); os.execvp('jq',['jq']); os.spawnlp(os.P_WAIT,'jq','jq'). All nine forms the file DOES claim to cover were verified present.
nonBlockingObservations.why: L-6 is scoped to 'a tool invoked through a name the AST cannot resolve to a literal argv[0]'. Every form above HAS a literal argv[0]; the gap is the enumerated API surface, not resolvability, so no published limit covers it. NON-BLOCKING under freeze section 7.1's own test: I swept the corpus and there are ZERO live occurrences of any of them, so no false accept is reachable on the frozen bytes. But the selection of what to widen was not principled -- os.system and os.popen were added with zero live sites, and subprocess.call, which is the oldest and simplest of these APIs and the substitution a future author is most likely to reach for, was not.

nonBlockingObservations.title: A TENTH undisclosed escape: NPA-3's subject set is scoped to artifacts named in BOTH documents, so DELETING a mention removes coverage instead of raising a finding.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: check_npa_3 selects subjects with `p.name in freeze_text and p.name in blueprint_text`. Step 1: I neutralised the REJECT tokens in the freeze blocks naming rust-provider-protocol.v2, leaving the name in both documents -- exit 1, subjectsGraded 30, subjectsRejected 4, 1 NPA-3-UNDISCLOSED-REJECT. Step 2: same un-disclosure, and additionally removed the artifact's name from IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md -- EXIT 0, subjectsGraded 30 -> 29, subjectsRejected 4 -> 3, ZERO findings.
nonBlockingObservations.why: The class is DEFINED as 'an artifact both package documents name', so by its own definition this is not a false negative. But its stated PURPOSE is that 'freeze section 2 rule 3 forbids implementing a REJECTED version, so a reader of that document alone cannot know' -- and after step 2 a reader of the freeze alone still cannot know, and nothing says so. The definition and the purpose diverge, and the divergence is reachable by an edit that makes the hazard MORE acute, not less. The banner does publish subjectsGraded, but nothing hard-compares it to anything, so a coverage drop is visible only to a reader who was already watching. Freeze section 7.2.2's rule -- a recorded measurement must be compared to the measurement it records -- is the available repair.

nonBlockingObservations.title: A NEGATIVE CONTROL can be silently reduced to a no-op by a corpus edit the instrument's own repair explicitly blesses.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: The modal-synonym control is `slice_text.replace("execution must follow", "execution shall follow", 1)`. I reworded the live CONTENT row in v1-slice.md from 'execution must follow' to 'execution IS REQUIRED TO follow' -- a form the widened NORMATIVE_MODAL vocabulary was extended to recognise, which keeps the grade CONTENT and the base GREEN. The control's replace then matches nothing, the overlay is byte-identical to the unmutated document, run_check re-runs the base, the case reports [SILENT], and the suite prints 'SELFTEST PASSED ... 3/3 negative controls silent' at exit 0 having tested nothing.
nonBlockingObservations.why: This is freeze section 7.2.2's rider -- a check that cannot fail the build is prose -- occurring inside the instrument that gates its own LIMITS count against exactly this failure. The asymmetry is the interesting part and it is worth stating precisely: the POSITIVE cases are fail-safe, because a no-op mutation produces no finding and is reported [ADMITTED] as an escape. Only the NEGATIVE controls are exposed, because for them silence is the pass condition and a no-op is indistinguishable from a genuine non-firing. A control that asserted its own mutation actually changed the bytes would close it in one line.

nonBlockingObservations.title: One selftest fixture is keyed on a live corpus identifier and is DROPPED SILENTLY when it disappears, unlike its three siblings which all refuse the run by name.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: The 'Readers must note:' control searches v1-slice.md for a table row naming `P-1` and is appended only `if p1_row is not None`. I performed the complete P-1 repair the instrument's own NPA-2 text prescribes -- removed both v1-slice.md lines naming P-1 and withdrew its section 5.1 register row. Base stays GREEN (disagreementsDerived 2, disagreementsRecorded 2), the suite reports 'SELFTEST PASSED' at exit 0, and the negative-control count silently goes 3 -> 2.
nonBlockingObservations.why: Three sibling fixtures -- the unresolved heading, the environment-section checker name, and the NPA-3 REJECT subject -- each get an explicit SELFTEST-NOT-RUN guard that refuses the run and says why. This one gets none. The published count is derived from len(negatives) so the DISCLOSURE does not go stale, which is a real mitigation; what goes missing without announcement is the CASE. `P-1` is also the only live corpus identifier written into a predicate anywhere in the file, which makes this the single surviving instance of the shape freeze section 7.8.1 warns about -- minor, because the fixture is a control rather than a defect site, but it is the one place the derivation discipline was not applied.

nonBlockingObservations.title: An ungated internal figure is stale by 2 -- the class the file gates elsewhere.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: Two comments state the suite's cost: line 415 '--selftest performs 25 complete runs' and line 873 '--selftest's 25 runs'. I wrapped run_check and counted: 27 complete invocations (1 base + 13 positives + 3 negatives + 10 hostile).
nonBlockingObservations.why: Cosmetic in effect -- the figures justify two caches and nothing depends on them. Recorded because the file makes a point of this exact discipline, gating its LIMITS count in both directions so 'the disclosure cannot go stale', and then leaves two of its own measurements uncompared. The suite grew by the two cases the repairs added and the comments did not follow.

nonBlockingObservations.title: 'Only this code means finding' is not true of the file's own exit table.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: The exit-code table says of 1: 'the check RAN COMPLETELY and found something. Only this code means finding.' But classify() makes INCOMPLETE dominate FINDINGS, and I measured two runs that exit 4 while carrying real findings: v1-slice.md absent plus a planted blueprint disagreement (exit 4, NPA-1 reported), and pin drift plus a planted undeclared tool (exit 4, NPA-4 reported).
nonBlockingObservations.why: The BEHAVIOUR is right and is the better choice -- a partial run reported as '1 finding' understates how much of the instrument was measuring. The row for exit 4 says so two lines later: 'Findings from the classes that DID run are still printed and are still real'. It is the sentence on the exit-1 row that is wrong, and a CI rule written from it ('exit 1 means findings') will miss findings that arrive at exit 4.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The subject's immunity to the closure filename heuristic is incidental rather than designed.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: The heuristic is `re.search(r"['\"]" + re.escape(other) + r"['\"]", src)` -- a quote IMMEDIATELY before the peer's filename. The subject's own constant is PCM = "artifacts/check-package-coherence.py", where the character preceding `check-` is `/`, not a quote. It escapes on the path prefix alone. The other four peer filenames in the file sit inside backticks in prose and escape for the same kind of reason.
nonBlockingObservations.why: No live consequence: the subject excludes itself from its own census, and I verified the predecessor's census over a source set including the subject attributes zero edges to it. Recorded because the author's stated repair for this regression was to DERIVE fixtures rather than name files, and this particular escape is not that repair -- an author writing `PCM_NAME = "check-package-coherence.py"` reintroduces the phantom edge against any instrument reusing the heuristic, including the predecessor, which is still live in the corpus.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The docstring inherits freeze section 7.8.1's overstatement of what the predecessor's RUN produces.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: The docstring says 'with v1-slice.md absent, derive_disagreements swallowed the OSError and THE RUN PRODUCED 3 false NPA-2-STALE-DISAGREEMENT-RECORD findings'. The finding SET is exactly right -- I reproduced all three by calling evaluate() directly. THE RUN produces none of them: main() prints a banner that re-reads the same six paths with the same call, so it raises before the FINDINGS block on every one of the five reachable disk states I tested.
nonBlockingObservations.why: NON-BLOCKING and arguably not the subject's fault -- it is repeating a standing freeze section, and the underlying defect it motivates is entirely real. Recorded for two reasons. First, section 7.8.1 was written FROM this incident and is now a binding rule, so the distinction between what an ANALYSIS computes and what a RUN emits should be exact in it. Second, the true shape is more instructive than the recorded one: the predecessor does fabricate three specific accusations from an absent input, and is prevented from publishing them only because a SECOND defect crashes first. 'A missing input can present as a substantive finding against a different artifact' remains true as a class; on these particular bytes it presents as a bare traceback, and an instrument saved from one defect by another is not safe, it is lucky.

whatIDidNotCheck: I did not audit check-package-coherence.py's review-state derivation. NPA-3's verdicts depend on pcm.review_state_of() and pcm.REVIEW_MARKERS, and I took both as given. I verified the PIN and its drift behaviour -- that the hash is computed before the bytes run, that the cache is keyed on the digest rather than the path so an overlay cannot be served a module built from other bytes, and that drift produces a named skip at exit 4 with five classes still measuring -- but NOT that the derivation it executes is correct. If review_state_of() is wrong, subjectsRejected is wrong and NPA-3 is wrong with it, and nothing in this review would have seen that.

I did not verify that freeze section 5.1's register is SUBSTANTIVELY correct -- that the three recorded disagreements are the right three, or that their CONTENT/STATUS grades are the right grades. I verified only that the derived set and the recorded set are hard-compared in both directions, which is all the instrument claims.

I did not verify the SEMANTICS of NPA-5 or NPA-6. I checked the plumbing -- that the referenceDerivation is resolved by shape rather than key name, that signatures are rendered from the executed module and compared to the blueprint text, that preimage completeness is recomputed and compared to the recorded figure in both directions. I did not check that check-d9-v1.14.py's exports actually implement the D9 axes-to-class oracle, nor that the PLAN-ID-V1 preimage field set is the right field set. Those are contract questions and this is an instrument review.

I did not read the predecessor's independent review artifact. I deliberately re-measured the predecessor's three adjudicated defects directly rather than checking the subject against a prior reviewer's account of them, so nothing here inherits that review's framing -- including its scoping, which is why the fourth defect went unrecorded there.

I did NOT exhaustively enumerate the instrument's falsifiable surface. The four successor instruments in freeze section 7.8 publish leaf-level counts (177 of 401 value-bound, 432 of 989, and so on); I did no equivalent sweep. My limit hunt was TARGETED -- I read the code for trust boundaries and probed the three or four most promising -- and it found two undisclosed routes in a few hours. The published figure of eight should therefore be read as a FLOOR that is now known to be at least ten, and nobody should read my two as the last two.

I did not test concurrency or TOCTOU beyond observing that the predecessor's banner and analysis read the same paths at different times. The subject caches disk bytes per process, which makes a mid-run edit invisible to it; I did not probe whether that is exploitable.

I did not test on any platform other than macOS with CPython 3.14.6. The AST predicate depends on ast node shapes that are version-sensitive in principle, and I did not check it against another Python version.

I did not verify the accuracy of IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md or IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md generally. I checked exactly the passages the adjudications required -- section 7.8.1's account of the predecessor, the environment-prerequisites section's table and prose, and section 7.6's list of five editable checkers -- and nothing else.

I did not re-run the corpus sweep against the drifted freeze. Every figure in the corpusBaseline block was taken against the dispatch snapshot 1e21c880...; six checkers in that sweep read the freeze and could in principle move.

scope: This reviews an INSTRUMENT, not the package it measures. It says nothing about whether the three recorded disagreements in freeze section 5.1 are acceptable, nor whether v1-slice.md should be amended -- section 2's authority order settles the first and section 10 the second, and the instrument is right to hold no opinion about either. What it does say is that the instrument's six classes fire, that its refusals are named and its exit codes true, that all three adjudicated repairs are real and were re-derived here rather than read, and that its published account of its own escape surface is incomplete by at least two routes -- one of which it positively denies.
